subject: POC kickoff recap: Redwood + Acme — scope, metrics, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC discussion — Redwood x Acme (next steps)

Hi Jordan / Lena —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Pain points you shared:
- Inconsistent latency on customer-facing generative features during peak traffic (up to ~2.5s p95).
- High per-token cost from current pipeline and duplicated inference across services.
- Lack of visibility into per-route token and latency breakdowns for engineering teams.

Primary goals for the POC (what success looks like):
1) Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by at least 30% while maintaining parity on top-line quality metrics.
2) Achieve p95 latency <= 800ms for typical 256-token calls under your baseline traffic shape.
3) Provide telemetry (per-route token counts, p95/p50 latency, and error rates) and a short eval set integration to detect regressions.

Proposed POC scope (high level):
- Duration: 6 weeks (kickoff this week if possible).
- Workloads: 2 production routes + 1 synthetic eval prompt set (we’ll work with your team to assemble).
- Deliverables: config + rollout plan, telemetry dashboard, cost comparison report, quality evals on your prompt set.

Immediate next steps:
1) I’ve attached a short scope doc and an access checklist (redwood-poc-scope.pdf, poc-access-checklist.xlsx).
2) Jordan — can you confirm the AWS account we’ll use for private workload routing and who on your side owns dataset access?
3) Dev (cc’d) will reach out to coordinate VPC peering and API keys once we have the account details.
4) We’ll sign the minimal SOW after we agree on scope — I’ve attached the signed NDA for completeness (acme-nda-signed.pdf).

If this looks good, I’ll schedule the kickoff for Thursday 3/12 at 10am PT. If that doesn’t work, please propose alternate times.

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Subject: POC kickoff recap + owners, metrics, timeline (official)

Hi all —

Per our confirmations, below is the formal POC kickoff recap and owner list so we have a single source of truth before Thursday’s call. Please review and reply with any corrections.

POC Name: Redwood-hosted inference POC for Acme — March 2026
Duration: 6 weeks (Mar 12 — Apr 23)
Kickoff call: Thu, Mar 12, 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent)

Scope (detailed):
- Ingest and serve two production routes: 
  1) customer_chat_api (primary user-facing generative route; ~256 tokens avg)
  2) internal_assist_api (internal knowledge helper; ~128 tokens avg)
- Integrate with Acme’s anonymized prompt set (200 examples + 50 edge cases) for quality evals.
- Autoscaling and cost profile assessment under your baseline traffic shape.
- Implement telemetry export (per-route token counts, p50/p95 latency, error rate) to a shared dashboard.

Primary success metrics:
- Cost: >= 30% reduction in $/1M tokens vs current baseline (measured across routes).
- Latency: p95 <= 800ms for customer_chat_api at baseline traffic.
- Quality: automated evals show no >5% drop in key quality signals (top-1 relevance & toxicity checks) on the agreed prompt set.

Prompt set / evals: 
- Acme to deliver: 200 anonymized prompts + expected outputs / acceptance criteria (Jordan).
- Redwood will run: baseline inference on current model + candidate optimized model(s) and provide an evaluation report.

Owners / contacts: 
- Acme: Jordan Smith (Product Eng, primary), Lena Ortiz (Data Owner)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program lead), Aditya Rao (Sales Engineer, model/config), Dev Patel (SRE/infra lead)

Technical access & setup steps (action items):
1) Acme: Add dev_patel@redwood.com to AWS account 987654321 with temporary admin for VPC peering and role setup. (Jordan)
2) Acme: Share S3 bucket path for anonymized prompt set + sample logs. (Jordan / Lena)
3) Redwood: Provide API keys and a staging environment URL; confirm network connectivity via VPC peering. (Dev)
4) Both: Agree on test traffic shape and schedule a load run in week 3 of the POC. (Aditya / Jordan)

Timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (Mar 12): Kickoff, infra access, initial data handoff
- Week 1: Baseline capture (current model serving) + initial Redwood staging setup
- Week 2: Run evals on prompt set; iterate model/config suggestions
- Week 3: Load testing and autoscaling validation
- Week 4-5: Fine-tuning config + rollback/run A/B where needed
- Week 6 (Apr 23): Final report, cost comparison, and recommendations

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope.pdf, poc-access-checklist.xlsx

If all good, we’ll proceed with the kickoff as scheduled. Aditya / Dev — can you call out any additional infra pre-reqs before the Thursday call?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks — quick infra checklist/notes from my side before kickoff: 

1) AWS account: 987654321 — please create a role named RedwoodPOCAdmin with trust to our account (123456789) and attach AdministratorAccess for the duration of the POC. We’ll rotate keys immediately after testing.
2) VPC peering: we’ll need CIDR ranges for peering verification; please confirm the VPC id.
3) S3 access: provide a presigned URL or an IAM policy for the prompt set bucket. We recommend presigned URL for the initial handoff to avoid long-lived creds.
4) Network egress: allow outbound to our telemetry endpoint (telemetry.redwood.com) on TCP 443.
5) Sample data: JSONL format preferred for prompt/eval entries; include expected output fields where possible.

I’ll open a ticket in our tracker with the above and send calendar invites for the infra sync pre-kickoff (30m) — proposed: Wed 3/11 11am PT. If your infra folks can join that would be ideal.

\u0014 Dev
Dev Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
